    17	import FormalConjecturesUtil
    18	
    19	/-!
    20	# Jacobson Conjecture
    21	
    22	*References:*
    23	- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobson's_conjecture)
    24	- [He1965]: Herstein, I. N. (1965), "A counterexample in Noetherian rings",
    25	  Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, 54 (4): 1036–1037
    26	  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC219788/
    27	- [Ja1956]: Jacobson, Nathan. Structure of rings. Vol. 37. American Mathematical Soc., 1956.
    28	- [Le1977]: Lenagan, T. H. (1977), "Noetherian rings with Krull dimension one",
    29	  J. London Math. Soc. Series 2, 15 (1): 41–47
    30	  https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/jlms/s2-15.1.41
    31	-/
    32	
    33	open Ring
    34	
    35	universe u
    36	
    37	namespace Jacobson
    38	
    39	/-- The Jacobson conjecture for a ring $R$: the infimum of the powers of the Jacobson radical
    40	$J$ is the zero ideal. -/
    41	def JacobsonConjectureFor (R : Type u) [Ring R] : Prop :=
    42	  ⨅ n : ℕ, jacobson R ^ n = 0
    43	
    44	/-- The Jacobson conjecture (in its modern form):
    45	In a (noncommutative) ring which is left and right Noetherian,
    46	the intersection of the powers of the Jacobson ideal is trivial -/
    47	@[category research open, AMS 16]
    48	theorem jacobson_conjecture :
    49	    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R],
    50	      JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
    51	  sorry
    52	
    53	/-- For commutative rings this is the case as a consequence of Krull's intersection theorem. -/
    54	@[category textbook, AMS 13 16]
    55	theorem jacobson_conjecture_of_comm_ring (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    56	    JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
    57	  sorry
    58	
    59	/-- Originally, on page 200 of [Ja1956], Jacobson asked if the Jacobson conjecture holds for all right
    60	Noetherian rings. However in [He1965] Herstein constructs a right Noetherian ring for which the
    61	Jacobson conjecture does not hold. -/
    62	@[category research solved, AMS 16]
    63	theorem jacobson_conjecture_of_right_noetherian :
    64	    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R], JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
    65	  sorry
    66	
    67	/- In [Le1977] Lenagan shows the Jacobson conjecture holds for left and right Noetherian rings
    68	with Krull dimension $1$. -/
    69	-- TODO: Add this result. Note that we do not have Krull dimension for noncommutative rings yet.
    70	
    71	end Jacobson
